drills.title: Does sizeof increment x?
drills.promptMd: Predict what the two lines print. Think about whether `sizeof` actually runs the expression inside it.
drills.explanationMd: `sizeof` only needs to determine the *type* of its operand — it never evaluates the expression. Because the expression is left unevaluated, the side effect `x++` never happens. The first line prints the size of `int` (typically `4`), and `x` stays `1`.

drills.title: Is -1 less than 1u?
drills.promptMd: What does this program print? Think about how C++ finds a common type for the comparison.
drills.explanationMd: When a signed `int` and an `unsigned int` are compared, C++ converts the signed value to `unsigned` to find a common type. `-1` converted to `unsigned int` becomes `4294967295` (on a 32-bit system), which is *not* less than `1`. The usual compiler warning (`-Wsign-compare`) is the hint this is happening — heed it.

drills.title: Fix the integer-division average
drills.promptMd: The function returns the wrong result for non-divisible inputs. Fix it so the average is computed as a true floating-point quotient.
drills.explanationMd: Both operands are `int`, so `total / count` performs *integer* division — the fractional part is discarded before the result is widened to `double`. The fix casts the dividend to `double` *before* the division: `static_cast<double>(total) / count` makes the entire operation floating-point from the start, preserving the fractional part.

drills.title: Guard before casting to size_t
drills.promptMd: Implement `isValidIndex` using `if` statements. Check that `index` is nonnegative first — only then is it safe to cast it to `std::size_t` for the upper-bound comparison.
drills.explanationMd: The sign check `if (index < 0) return false;` must come first. Only after confirming the value is nonnegative is it safe to `static_cast<std::size_t>(index)` for the upper-bound comparison — casting a negative `int` to an unsigned type yields a gigantic value that sails right past any length check, silently accepting an invalid index.

drills.title: Fix the unsigned wraparound in remaining()
drills.promptMd: The function wraps to a huge number instead of returning `0` when more items are taken than exist. Fix it so the result is clamped to zero when `taken` exceeds `total`.
drills.explanationMd: `std::size_t` is unsigned, so it cannot represent negative numbers — when `taken` exceeds `total`, the subtraction wraps around to a very large value instead of going below zero. The fix guards with `if (taken >= total) return 0;` before performing the subtraction, ensuring the operation only runs when the result is representable.
